app.title: The Devolution-Productivity Observatory
overview.sub: {region} · {n_fua} functional urban areas in the OECD data
overview.reading.title: Reading the Observatory
overview.reading.1: [Productivity](view:productivity) ranks {possessive} FUAs by labour productivity, compares them with every other country's, and follows the spread of productivity over time. [Autonomy](view:autonomy) traces the Local Autonomy Index and the Regional Authority Index. [Map](view:map) draws productivity, population and autonomy indicators for any year at national, TL2, TL3 or FUA level; the geography is chosen in the top bar.
overview.reading.2: Every chart can be shown as a table and downloaded as CSV. Dollar figures are nominal USD at purchasing power parity, comparable across countries within a year. Dollar values are not adjusted for inflation across time.
overview.table.title: Functional urban areas in {country}
overview.table.intro: Functional urban areas (FUAs) are the OECD's definition of a city and its commuting zone. The table summarises those in {country} at the years shown. Only FUAs for which the OECD publishes both GDP and labour productivity are counted; population and GDP are each taken from the year shown. Dollar figures are nominal USD at purchasing power parity: comparable across countries within a year, not across years.
overview.table.none: The OECD publishes no functional urban area GDP or labour productivity for {country}.
overview.measure.pop_share: Combined FUA population, share of national population
overview.measure.gdp_share: Combined FUA GDP, share of national GDP
overview.table.note.threshold: The OECD disseminates FUA labour productivity for areas of 250,000 inhabitants or more; the threshold is applied when FUAs are classified, not to each year's population.
overview.table.note.small: Measured population dips below it in {n_small} of the {n_shown} area-years shown, the smallest being {fua} at {pop} in {year}.
overview.table.note.interp: Population is interpolated or carried from a neighbouring year for {which} area-years shown.
overview.table.note.sources: See [Sources](view:sources) for how the series are combined.
overview.nat.title: National labour productivity, by country
overview.nat.intro: The nation-wide series behind the comparisons that follow: {country} is drawn in red, the other countries in the colours used throughout the Observatory.
overview.nat.note: OECD Productivity Database: GDP per person employed at chain-linked volumes, PPP-converted. The shaded band is the WHO pandemic emergency (March 2020 to May 2023).

productivity.ranks.none: Labour productivity data are not available for {country} in {year}.
productivity.scatter.title: Labour productivity and population of functional urban areas, {year}
productivity.scatter.intro: Each point is one functional urban area in {year}; point size is proportional to population. Red points are FUAs in {country}, grey the FUAs of the other countries. The labelled FUAs are the highest, median and lowest labour productivity in {country} (red) and across all countries (grey). The dataset holds {n_fua} FUAs with productivity and population across {n_countries} countries.
productivity.scatter.trend: Trend lines show the relationship between population size and labour productivity for all FUAs (dashed) and for {possessive} FUAs alone (red). The mean productivity of all FUAs and of {possessive} FUAs are drawn as horizontal reference lines.
productivity.scatter.nat: For comparison, {possessive} nation-wide labour productivity in {year} was {value} per person employed.
productivity.scatter.nat_only: {possessive} nation-wide labour productivity in {year} was {value} per person employed; the OECD publishes no FUA productivity for {country} in {year}.
productivity.r2.title: Population size and labour productivity: R² by country
productivity.r2.intro: The length of each bar shows how much of the variation in FUA labour productivity within a country is associated with population size. Population size is strongly associated with productivity in France and, to a lesser degree, the United States, but hardly at all elsewhere: productivity is not directly a function of urban agglomeration.
productivity.r2.note: R² of labour productivity on log10(population) across each country's FUAs, in each country's most recent year with productivity data.
productivity.dist.title: Distribution of FUA labour productivity, by country
productivity.dist.intro: The box edges mark the 25th and 75th percentiles of FUA labour productivity in each country, the solid line the median and the dashed line the mean. The United States has the widest spread; the other countries are narrowly clustered with some high-productivity outliers.
productivity.dist.note: Each country's most recent year with productivity data. Box: 25th to 75th percentile; solid line: median; dashed line: mean.
productivity.growth.title: Change in FUA labour productivity, {start} to {year}
productivity.growth.intro: FUAs ranked by the compound annual growth rate of labour productivity between {start} and {year}.
productivity.growth.ends: The series ends in {ref_year}, the last full year before the Covid-19 pandemic.
productivity.growth.begins: It begins in {start}, the first year OECD labour productivity data are available for {country}.
productivity.growth.none: Insufficient data to calculate productivity growth for {country} over 2004–{year}.
productivity.spread.title: Spread of FUA labour productivity in {country}
productivity.spread.intro: Percentiles of labour productivity across {possessive} FUAs in each year: a narrowing of the spread would indicate convergence across FUAs.
productivity.spread.covers: The figure covers the {n} years for which the OECD publishes productivity for {country} ({first}–{last}).
productivity.spread.few: The OECD publishes {how_many} of productivity for {country}, so only the cross-country comparison below is shown.
productivity.spread.note: The shaded band is the WHO pandemic emergency (March 2020 to May 2023).
productivity.cov.title: Coefficient of variation of FUA labour productivity, by country
productivity.cov.note: Standard deviation as a share of the mean across each country's FUAs, as published by the OECD. The shaded band is the WHO pandemic emergency.
productivity.mean.title: Mean FUA labour productivity, by country
productivity.mean.note: Mean values are unweighted: each FUA counts once, regardless of population. The shaded band is the WHO pandemic emergency.
autonomy.title: Local and regional autonomy · {country}
autonomy.sub: Local Autonomy Index (1990–2020) and Regional Authority Index (1950–2018), scaled 0–1
autonomy.lai.title: Local Autonomy Index, total score
autonomy.lai.intro: The Local Autonomy Index project calculates an indicator of the political, policy and fiscal autonomy of local government in a range of Global North countries. The composite indicator is shown for 1990–2020.
autonomy.lai_fiscal.title: Local Autonomy Index, fiscal score
autonomy.lai_fiscal.intro: The fiscal dimension of the LAI combines four sub-indicators: fiscal autonomy (independent power to tax), the financial transfer system (unconditionality of transfers received), financial self-reliance (reliance on own-source revenue) and borrowing autonomy (independent power to borrow).
autonomy.lai_fiscal.note: Sub-indicators are summed with the index's own point weights (4, 3, 3, 3) and rescaled to 0–1.
autonomy.rai.title: Regional Authority Index, total score
autonomy.rai.intro: The Regional Authority Index measures the self-rule and shared rule of regional governments from 1950 to 2018. Where the LAI assesses the autonomy of local governments, the RAI evaluates the autonomy of regional governments such as cantons, provinces, states or Länder: a federal country with strong provinces but weak local government may score high on the RAI and low on the LAI.
autonomy.rai.note: National values are population-weighted means of regional scores, rescaled here to 0–1 from the published 0–30 scale.
autonomy.rai_fiscal.title: Regional Authority Index, fiscal score
autonomy.rai_fiscal.intro: The fiscal dimension of the RAI combines two sub-indicators: fiscal autonomy (independent power to tax) and borrowing autonomy (independent power to borrow).
autonomy.rai_fiscal.note: Sub-indicators are summed with the index's own point weights (4 and 3) and rescaled to 0–1; national values are population-weighted means of regional scores.

sources.combine.title: How the sources are combined
sources.combine.1: The OECD publishes each indicator on its own schedule, so the sources above are joined on functional urban area and year without privileging any one of them: an observation is kept whether or not the other series cover the same year.
sources.combine.2: Population is the exception that needs handling, because it is what the other indicators are weighted and scaled by. It is disseminated annually for most countries but only at five-year census intervals for others, Japan most notably, where the published productivity year (2021) falls outside the census series entirely. Population is therefore linearly interpolated between observations within each functional urban area, and the nearest observation is carried forward or backward by at most three years beyond the observed range.
sources.combine.pop: Of the {total} functional urban area population values used for {country}, {observed} are as published by the OECD, {interpolated} interpolated and {carried} carried from the nearest observed year.

about.title: About the Observatory
about.tagline: Labour productivity of functional urban areas and the autonomy of local and regional government in nine countries.
about.what.title: What it shows
about.what.1: The Devolution-Productivity Observatory presents, for Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Spain, the United Kingdom and the United States, the labour productivity of OECD functional urban areas (a city and its commuting zone) alongside two expert-coded measures of subnational autonomy: the Local Autonomy Index and the Regional Authority Index. It is the interactive counterpart of the country profile documents produced for the Devolution project, and draws every figure from the same data pack.
about.what.2: Each view follows the profile: an [Overview](view:overview) of a country's FUAs; [Productivity](view:productivity) rankings, the relationship with population size, the distribution and spread of productivity across FUAs and its change over time; the [Autonomy](view:autonomy) indices; and a [Map](view:map) of any indicator in any year at four geographies: countries, large regions (TL2), small regions (TL3) and functional urban areas, chosen in the top bar. The country is chosen in the top bar; the URL carries every selection, so any view can be linked.
about.method.title: Method
about.method.1: OECD series are retrieved from the OECD Data Explorer SDMX API and joined on functional urban area and year. Population is interpolated between census observations and carried by at most three years beyond them, as described under [Sources](view:sources). Dollar figures are nominal USD at purchasing power parity: comparable across countries within a year, not across years. The reference year for the snapshot views is {ref_year}, the last full year before the Covid-19 pandemic, and the pandemic emergency as defined by the World Health Organization (March 2020 to May 2023) is shaded on every time series.
about.method.2: Means across FUAs are unweighted: each FUA counts once, regardless of population. The fiscal dimensions of the LAI and RAI are sums of their sub-indicators using the indices' own point weights, rescaled to 0–1. The map classes each indicator into quantiles pooled over every year shown for the scope chosen, so a colour keeps its meaning as the year changes.
about.how.title: How it works
about.how.1: The site is static. The data are Parquet files segmented by country (one file per country for the FUA series, plus small national, LAI, RAI and source tables) and simplified boundaries (a TopoJSON per country holding its national outline, TL2 and TL3 regions, which share their borders, plus GeoJSON for FUAs), read in the browser by DuckDB-WASM. A country view fetches only that country's file; the cross-country comparisons read all nine. Everything the site shows can be downloaded as CSV from each chart, or read directly from the `data/` folder of the repository with any Parquet tool.

overview.reg.kpi.median.sub: GVA per worker, USD PPP (2020 prices)
overview.reg.table.title: {level} regions in {country}
overview.reg.table.intro: The table summarises labour productivity across the {level} regions of {country} at the years shown: how many regions the OECD reports, the median region, the 10th and 90th percentiles and their ratio, the coefficient of variation, and the median region's distance from the country's most productive region (the frontier). Productivity is gross value added per worker in US dollars at purchasing power parity and constant 2020 prices (OECD DF_LPR), so unlike the FUA figures it is comparable across years.
overview.reg.table.none: The OECD publishes no {level} labour productivity for {country}.
overview.reg.measure.ratio: Ratio of the 90th to the 10th percentile
overview.reg.measure.gap: Median gap to the frontier region
overview.reg.gap.title: Median {level} gap to the frontier region, by country
overview.reg.gap.intro: Each region's productivity as a percentage below the most productive region of its country, the median taken across the country's {level} regions in each year. A line rising towards zero means the typical region is closing on the frontier: convergence within the country.
overview.reg.gap.note: OECD DF_LPR, gap to the national frontier as computed in the regional panel. The shaded band is the WHO pandemic emergency (March 2020 to May 2023).
overview.reg.ratio.title: Spread of {level} productivity (P90/P10), by country
overview.reg.ratio.intro: The productivity of the region at the 90th percentile divided by that at the 10th, across the {level} regions of each country. A falling ratio means the more and less productive regions are drawing closer.
overview.reg.ratio.note: Countries with fewer than three regions in a year are left out. The shaded band is the WHO pandemic emergency.
overview.nat2.kpi.growth.sub: mean annual growth of GDP per worker, log points × 100
overview.nat2.kpi.cv.sub: coefficient of variation of regional productivity
overview.nat2.kpi.cv.none: no regional data at this level
overview.nat2.disp.title: Regional dispersion of productivity, by country
overview.nat2.disp.intro: How unequal labour productivity is across each country's regions, in the latest year with data: the coefficient of variation across TL2 and across TL3 regions, and the share of national employment in the most productive TL2 region. The [Productivity](view:productivity) view follows the dispersion over time.
overview.nat2.disp.note: Computed in the devo_data_pack national panel from OECD DF_LPR regional productivity. The year of each value is in brackets.
productivity.reg.sub: {level} regions, GVA per worker in USD at purchasing power parity, constant 2020 prices
productivity.reg.ranks.title: {level} regions by labour productivity, {year}
productivity.reg.ranks.intro: The top ten, middle ten and bottom ten {level} regions in {country} by labour productivity in {year}{ref_clause}. Separator rows are omitted where the groups are contiguous.
productivity.reg.scatter.title: Labour productivity and population of {level} regions, {year}
productivity.reg.scatter.intro: Each point is one {level} region in {year}; point size is proportional to population. Red points are regions of {country}, grey the regions of the other countries. The labelled regions are the highest, median and lowest labour productivity in {country} (red) and across all countries (grey). The dataset holds {n_fua} regions with productivity and population across {n_countries} countries.
productivity.reg.scatter.trend: Trend lines show the relationship between population and labour productivity for all regions (dashed) and for {possessive} regions alone (red). The mean productivity of all regions and of {possessive} regions are drawn as horizontal reference lines.
productivity.reg.scatter.nat_only: {possessive} nation-wide labour productivity in {year} was {value} per person employed; the OECD publishes no {level} productivity for {country} in {year}.
productivity.reg.r2.intro: The length of each bar shows how much of the variation in labour productivity across a country's {level} regions is associated with population size. Regions are administrative units, not labour markets, so population measures size less cleanly than it does for FUAs.
productivity.reg.r2.note: R² of labour productivity on log10(population) across each country's {level} regions, in each country's most recent year with productivity data.
productivity.reg.dist.title: Distribution of {level} labour productivity, by country
productivity.reg.dist.intro: The box edges mark the 25th and 75th percentiles of labour productivity across each country's {level} regions, the solid line the median and the dashed line the mean; each dot is a region.
productivity.reg.growth.title: Change in {level} labour productivity, {start} to {year}
productivity.reg.growth.intro: {level} regions ranked by the compound annual growth rate of labour productivity between {start} and {year}. The series are at constant prices, so growth here is real growth.
productivity.reg.spread.title: Spread of {level} labour productivity in {country}
productivity.reg.spread.intro: Percentiles of labour productivity across {possessive} {level} regions in each year: a narrowing of the spread would indicate convergence across regions.
productivity.reg.cov.title: Coefficient of variation of {level} labour productivity, by country
productivity.reg.cov.note: Standard deviation as a share of the mean across each country's {level} regions, unweighted, computed here from OECD DF_LPR. The shaded band is the WHO pandemic emergency.
productivity.reg.mean.title: Mean {level} labour productivity, by country
productivity.reg.mean.note: Mean values are unweighted: each region counts once, regardless of population or employment. The shaded band is the WHO pandemic emergency.
productivity.nat.sub: National series: productivity, its growth, and its dispersion across regions
productivity.nat.lp.title: National labour productivity, by country
productivity.nat.lp.intro: GDP per person employed or per hour worked, at constant prices and purchasing power parity, for the nine countries: {country} in red.
productivity.nat.lp.note: OECD Productivity Database, as carried in the devo_data_pack national panel. The shaded band is the WHO pandemic emergency (March 2020 to May 2023).
productivity.nat.decomp.title: Growth of GDP per capita and its sources, {country}
productivity.nat.decomp.intro: Each year's growth of {possessive} GDP per capita (the black line) split into the growth of GDP per person employed (labour productivity) and the growth of persons employed per head of population. In log points the two parts add up exactly to the total.
productivity.nat.decomp.note: Annual log differences × 100 of the OECD Productivity Database series; the employment part is the GDP per capita growth less the GDP per worker growth.
productivity.nat.decomp.none: No growth series is available for {country}.
productivity.nat.avg.title: Sources of growth in GDP per capita, {first}–{last}, by country
productivity.nat.avg.intro: The same decomposition as the mean annual growth over {first}–{last}, countries ordered by GDP per capita growth (the dot); {country} is drawn at full strength.
productivity.nat.rd.title: Dispersion of productivity across {level} regions, by country
productivity.nat.rd.intro: The coefficient of variation of labour productivity across each country's {level} regions, year by year: a falling line means the country's regions are converging.
productivity.nat.rd.note: Computed in the devo_data_pack national panel from OECD DF_LPR regional productivity. The shaded band is the WHO pandemic emergency.
productivity.nat.rd.no_tl3: The OECD publishes no TL3 productivity for {country}.
autonomy.nat.dims.title: Decentralization dimension indices, by country
autonomy.nat.dims.intro: Three composite indices of decentralization, fiscal, administrative and political, each standardized across countries and years (z-scores: 0 is the mean, 1 a standard deviation above it). Choose the dimension above the chart.
autonomy.nat.dims.note: Dimension indices of the devo_data_pack national panel, 1990–2018.
autonomy.nat.fiscal.title: Fiscal decentralization ratios, by country
autonomy.nat.fiscal.intro: The subnational share of general government expenditure, revenue and tax revenue (IMF Fiscal Decentralization dataset), and the share of subnational tax revenue over which subnational governments have discretion (OECD tax autonomy). Choose the ratio above the chart.
autonomy.nat.fiscal.note: IMF Fiscal Decentralization dataset and OECD Fiscal Decentralisation Database, as carried in the devo_data_pack national panel. The IMF reports no expenditure share for France or Italy.
autonomy.reg.sub: Region-specific Local Autonomy Index (0–1, 1990–2020) and Regional Authority Index (points, 1990–2018), {level} regions
autonomy.reg.reading: Each chart draws every {level} region of {country} as a faint line, the median across regions dashed and the region chosen at the top right in red. The LAI is scored 0–1. The RAI is in raw points summed over every tier of government that governs the region, so a region under several tiers can score above any single tier's maximum; it is not on the 0–1 scale of the national charts. Berlin, Bremen and Hamburg are not coded in LAI 2.0.
autonomy.reg.uniform: Region-specific LAI is the same in every region of {country}: it varies only where municipal types differ in their population shares (Spain, Japan and France).
autonomy.reg.csv_all: Download every {level} region's LAI and RAI (CSV)
autonomy.reg.none: No region-specific values are available for {country}.
autonomy.reg.lai.title: Local Autonomy Index by {level} region
autonomy.reg.lai.intro: The autonomy of the local governments within each {level} region. Where municipal types differ (Spain, Japan and France) it is the LAI of each type weighted by the share of the region's population it governs; elsewhere it follows the country's value.
autonomy.reg.lai.note: LAI 2.0 mapped to regions in the devo_data_pack crosswalk (lai_region_tl), 0–1.
autonomy.reg.lai_fiscal.title: Local Autonomy Index, fiscal, by {level} region
autonomy.reg.lai_fiscal.intro: The fiscal dimension of local autonomy (taxing, transfers, self-reliance and borrowing) for the local governments within each {level} region.
autonomy.reg.rai.title: Regional Authority Index by {level} region
autonomy.reg.rai.intro: The self-rule and shared rule of the regional governments over each {level} region, summed over every regional tier (Bavaria in 2018: Land 27, Regierungsbezirk 10 and Bezirk 10, 47 in all).
autonomy.reg.rai.note: RAI mapped to regions in the devo_data_pack crosswalk (rai_region_tl), raw points summed over tiers. Regions with no regional government have no value.
autonomy.reg.rai_fiscal.title: Regional Authority Index, fiscal autonomy, by {level} region
autonomy.reg.rai_fiscal.intro: The independent power of the regional governments over each {level} region to tax, summed over tiers in raw points.
